meta.syntheticNote: Every entity, claim, and figure on this page is generated from the seed above. Nothing derives from any real book of business.
meta.$comment: Parameters and planted anomalies only. The ~1,900-claim population is synthesized deterministically at load time by assets/js/generate.js, which keeps this file reviewable and keeps the interesting rows explicit.

assumptions.label: Tail factor beyond 42 months
assumptions.note: Applied beyond the oldest observed development age. No credible tail can be fitted from four policy years — this is a judgment input, not a derived one.

assumptions.label: Annual severity trend
assumptions.note: Applied to on-level prior years for comparability. Set to zero to see the untrended comparison.

assumptions.label: Annual aggregate (renewal)
assumptions.note: The decision in front of the board. Move it to see the effect on projected headroom at expiry.

assumptions.label: Target capital margin over projected ultimate
assumptions.note: Surplus held above projected ultimate net liabilities.

reserving.name: Incurred chain ladder
reserving.description: Age-to-age factors are computed from this program's own incurred development triangle, then applied to project each policy year to ultimate. A judgment tail factor is applied beyond the oldest observed age.
reserving.citation: Standard actuarial reserving method. See Casualty Actuarial Society, 'Estimating Unpaid Claims Using Basic Techniques' (Friedland), Ch. 7.

method.note: Development factors are derived from the synthetic program's own data, not imported from an external benchmark. Nothing on this page cites an industry figure it cannot show the derivation for.

defects.label: Duplicate claim under variant identifiers
defects.description: The same claim appears in both source systems under a transcribed claim number and a different spelling of the insured entity. Naive ingest treats it as two claims and counts the reserve twice.

defects.label: Reserve movement with no effective date
defects.description: A case reserve change carries no effective date, so it cannot be assigned to a development period. Excluded from the triangle until dated.

defects.label: Coverage code outside the schema
defects.description: Free-text coverage codes from the TPA extract that do not map to the program's canonical codes.

defects.label: Insured entity name variants
defects.description: One insured appears under three spellings across the two source systems, splitting its experience across three apparent entities and distorting per-entity loss ratios.

defects.label: Paid exceeding per-occurrence retention
defects.description: Paid plus reserve exceeds the $500,000 per-occurrence retention. Either the excess layer was not applied on the extract, or the claim is genuinely above retention and was not ceded.

defects.label: Report date precedes occurrence date
defects.description: Impossible date ordering, usually a data-entry transposition. Distorts report-lag analysis and policy-year assignment on claims-made coverage.

narrative.assertion: Ingest read the internal register's PL-2026-0188 as a claim with no match in the TPA extract, and opened it as new. The claim number is one digit short of PL-2026-00188 and the insured is spelled differently in each system, so neither exact-match nor entity-match dedup caught it.
narrative.consequence: The claim's full incurred — paid indemnity, paid expense, and case reserve — was counted twice in reported incurred for policy year 2026.
narrative.magnification: Because the error sits at six months of development, the chain ladder multiplies it by the age-to-ultimate factor before it reaches the projection. The projection error is materially larger than the data error.
narrative.decisionImpact: Uncorrected, projected consumption of the 2026 aggregate reads above 100% — a projected breach, and the board is asked to approve a capital call. Corrected, the year projects inside the aggregate with headroom intact.
narrative.resolution: Flagged by identity resolution on normalized claim number and fuzzy entity match. Held for human confirmation rather than auto-merged: an auto-merge on a near-match claim number is exactly as dangerous as the duplicate.
narrative.confirmedBy: Claims operations, confirmed against the TPA's own claim file
